problemText: A polygon is being drawn from its vertices listed in order. After plotting all the vertices and connecting them to each other in sequence, what is the one final step you must do to complete the polygon?
choices: Check that all sides are either horizontal or vertical
Erase all the vertex points so only the sides show
Count the total number of sides to name the polygon
Connect the last vertex back to the first vertex
hints: The lesson emphasizes that a polygon must be closed with no loose ends.
Think about what makes a shape a complete polygon instead of just a connected path.

problemText: Two consecutive vertices of a polygon are at M(4, 7) and N(4, 2), where each unit is one inch. What type of side connects these vertices, and how can you tell?
choices: Vertical, because both vertices have the same first coordinate
Horizontal, because both vertices have the same first coordinate
Vertical, because both vertices have the same second coordinate
Diagonal, because the vertices do not share any coordinate
hints: Check which coordinate is the same for both M and N.
Remember: same first coordinate means the side runs straight up and down.

problemText: A parking lot outline has vertices at C(2, 5), D(8, 5), E(8, 1), and F(2, 1), listed in order. The parking lot manager needs to know the length of side CD. What is the length of side CD in units?
hints: First identify what coordinate C and D share.
Look at only the coordinate that differs, and use subtraction since both values are positive.

problemText: A decorative frame has vertices at P(-3, 2), Q(5, 2), R(5, -4), and S(-3, -4), listed in order. To draw this frame correctly, you need to identify each side and verify it is either horizontal or vertical. How many of the four sides are horizontal?
hints: A horizontal side connects vertices that share the same second coordinate.
Check each consecutive pair: P to Q, Q to R, R to S, and S back to P.

problemText: A walkway polygon has vertices at A(1, -6), B(1, 3), and C(7, 3). If you connect these vertices in order and then close the polygon by connecting C back to A, side AB runs vertically. Which statement correctly describes why you can find the length of AB using only the second coordinates?
choices: Because A and B have different first coordinates, the distance between them is determined by subtracting the first coordinates and ignoring the second coordinates
Because A and B share the same first coordinate, so the vertical distance depends only on the second coordinates
Because when the first coordinate stays constant at 1 for both points, you only need to find the distance between -6 and 3, which are the second coordinates
Because the first coordinate determines whether a side is vertical or horizontal, and once you know the side is vertical, the length comes from subtracting the second coordinates of the endpoints
hints: Look at the first coordinates of A(1, -6) and B(1, 3). Are they the same?
When a coordinate is fixed, the only measurement that changes along that line is the other coordinate.

problemText: A community plot is shaped like a trapezoid with vertices at V(-5, 3), W(-5, -2), X(4, -2), and Y(4, 3), listed in order. Each unit is one yard. To build a fence around the entire perimeter, you need to find the lengths of two adjacent sides: side VW and side WX. What is the sum of these two side lengths?
hints: Find which coordinate is shared by V and W, then which is shared by W and X.
For VW, watch whether the second coordinates are on the same side of zero or opposite sides. Do the same for WX using first coordinates.

problemText: A triangle has a base of 10 meters and a height of 8 meters, where the height is measured perpendicular to the base. What is the area of the triangle?
hints: Remember that area of a triangle equals base times height divided by two.
Start by multiplying the base and height together, then divide that product in half.

problemText: A parallelogram has a base of 12 inches. The straight up-and-down distance between the parallelogram's two parallel sides is 7 inches. One of the slanted sides of the parallelogram measures 9 inches. What is the area of the parallelogram?
hints: Think about which measurement tells you how tall the parallelogram is — perpendicular to the base.
The slanted side length is a distractor; you need the perpendicular distance, not the slant.

problemText: Marcus is drawing a triangle on grid paper. He chooses a base of the triangle that is 9 centimeters long. He measures the perpendicular distance from that base to the opposite corner and finds it is 6 centimeters. What is the area of Marcus's triangle, in square centimeters?
hints: Use the triangle area rule: base times height, then divide by two.
Make sure you divide by two after multiplying; that is the key step that makes it a triangle and not a rectangle.

problemText: A composite shape is made of a rectangle and a triangle sitting on top of it. The rectangle has a width of 6 inches and a height of 5 inches. On top of the rectangle, a triangle has the same 6-inch width as the rectangle's top edge for its base, and the triangle's height, measured perpendicular to that base, is 4 inches. What is the total area of the entire composite shape?
hints: Decompose the shape into two pieces: find the area of the rectangle and the area of the triangle separately.
Add the areas of the two pieces together to get the total area of the whole shape.

problemText: A trapezoid-shaped garden bed can be decomposed by drawing a vertical line from one corner of the shape to the opposite side. This creates a rectangle and a triangle. The rectangle part is 8 meters wide and 3 meters tall. The triangle part has a base of 2 meters and a height of 3 meters, measured perpendicular to its base. What is the total area of the garden bed?
hints: Find the area of the rectangle using length times width.
Find the area of the triangle using base times height divided by two, then add the two areas together.

problemText: A large rectangle is 10 inches wide and 8 inches tall. From one corner of the rectangle, a right triangle is cut away. The triangle has a base of 4 inches and a height of 8 inches, measured perpendicular to that base. You can think of the remaining shape as the big rectangle with a triangular piece removed. What is the area of the shape that remains after the triangle is cut away?
hints: Start by finding the area of the whole large rectangle before anything is removed.
Then find the area of the triangle that was cut away, and subtract it from the rectangle's area.

problemText: A net is a flat pattern that can be folded into a three-dimensional solid. Which statement correctly describes what happens to the faces of a solid when it is unfolded into its net?
choices: Each face of the solid is cut into smaller geometric pieces so that it can lay flat on paper, and these pieces are then scattered at random positions with no organized pattern.
Each face becomes a flat shape in the net, keeping its exact size and staying attached to at least one neighboring face along a shared edge.
Only the exterior surfaces of the solid become shapes in the net, while all interior faces remain hidden and do not appear in the unfolded pattern.
The faces are arranged in a circular formation around a central point in the net, positioned so that no edges of different faces touch or connect to one another.
hints: Think about what 'unfolding' a box means—do the faces get smaller or stay the same size?
Remember that in a net, neighboring faces stay connected because they shared an edge in the solid.

problemText: A rectangular prism has a net showing six rectangles. Two of the rectangles are 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. Two others are 5 cm long and 4 cm wide. The remaining two are 3 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is the total surface area of this rectangular prism?
hints: Start by finding the area of each pair of matching rectangles, using length times width for each.
Surface area is the sum of all six faces, so add the area of all three pairs together.

problemText: Marcus drew a net for a triangular prism. The net shows two identical right triangles with legs 6 inches and 8 inches, plus three rectangles: one that is 6 inches by 10 inches, one that is 8 inches by 10 inches, and one that is 10 inches by 10 inches. Which statement is correct?
choices: The net is drawn correctly in terms of shape and size, but the rectangles are placed in an order that prevents the faces from folding together properly into a solid.
The net is drawn wrong because the three rectangles do not all have the same height, which means they cannot wrap around the three different sides of the triangle correctly.
The net is drawn wrong because the two triangles should not be identical to each other; one must be larger than the other to form a valid triangular prism.
The net is drawn correctly because all three side lengths of the triangle (6, 8, and the third side) are matched to a rectangle of the correct width.
hints: For a triangular prism, each side of the triangle must wrap around its own rectangle—check that each rectangle's width matches a triangle side.
Use the Pythagorean relationship to find the third side of a right triangle with legs 6 and 8.

problemText: A gift box shaped like a rectangular prism measures 12 cm long, 8 cm wide, and 5 cm tall. The box will be wrapped in paper. To find how much paper is needed, you must find the total surface area. A student began by finding the area of the top face (12 × 8 = 96 square cm) and the area of the front face (12 × 5 = 60 square cm). Explain what the student must do next to correctly find the total surface area, and state the final answer.
choices: Find the area of the left end (8 × 5 = 40 square cm), then add all three different face areas and double the total: (96 + 60 + 40) × 2 = 392 square cm.
Add 96 and 60 to get 156 square cm, then multiply by the width to account for all faces that surround the box, since these two faces represent the only dimensions needed.

Find the area of the back face (12 × 5 = 60 square cm) and the bottom face (12 × 8 = 96 square cm), then add only the front and top: 96 + 60 + 60 + 96 = 312 square cm, because opposite faces don't need to be counted twice.
Find the area of the right end (8 × 5 = 40 square cm) and add it to the areas already found, then add the remaining side face area: 96 + 60 + 40 + 40 = 236 square cm.
hints: A rectangular prism has six faces in three matching pairs—make sure you account for all of them.
After finding the area of three different faces (top, front, and one end), what do you do with those three numbers to get the total for all six faces?

problemText: A triangular prism pencil case has two identical triangular ends that are right triangles with legs 5 cm and 12 cm. The pencil case is 8 cm long between its two triangular ends. First, find the area of one triangular end using the formula base × height ÷ 2. Then, find the total surface area of the pencil case by adding the area of both triangular ends and all three rectangular faces.
choices: The two triangular ends have a combined area of 30 square cm, plus the two rectangles (5 × 8) + (12 × 8) = 136 square cm, for a total of 166 square cm.
The two triangular ends have a combined area of 60 square cm, plus the three rectangles (5 × 8) + (12 × 8) + (13 × 8) = 240 square cm, for a total of 300 square cm.
The two triangular ends have a combined area of 120 square cm, plus the three rectangles (5 × 8) + (12 × 8) + (13 × 8) = 240 square cm, for a total of 360 square cm.
The two triangular ends have a combined area of 60 square cm, plus only the rectangle wrapping the longest side (13 × 8) = 104 square cm, for a total of 164 square cm.
hints: Use the Pythagorean relationship to find the third side of the right triangle with legs 5 and 12.
Every side of the triangle—all three—must wrap around its own rectangle; do not skip any rectangle face.

problemText: A net for a rectangular prism is laid out as follows: a horizontal strip of four rectangles, each 3 cm tall, in widths of 2 cm, 6 cm, 2 cm, and 6 cm from left to right. Two additional rectangles, each 6 cm by 3 cm, are attached to the top and bottom edges of the second rectangle in the strip. Before calculating surface area, carefully count the faces and confirm which dimension appears twice in matching pairs. Then calculate the total surface area.
choices: The six faces are arranged in two pairs of 2 × 3 rectangles and two pairs of 6 × 3 rectangles, with one pair appearing three times, for a total of 66 square cm.
The six faces form three pairs: two faces of 2 × 3, two of 6 × 3, and two of 6 × 3, for a total of 72 square cm.
The six faces are arranged in three pairs: 2 × 3 (area 6), 6 × 3 (area 18), and 6 × 3 (area 18), with each pair counted twice: (6 + 18 + 18) × 2 = 84 square cm.
The net contains only five faces total because the two attached rectangles overlap, so surface area cannot be calculated.
hints: Count carefully: the horizontal strip has four rectangles, and two more are attached, so the net should show six faces total for a rectangular prism.
A rectangular prism's six faces form three matching pairs; identify which dimension repeats to find the pairs, then double each pair's area and add them.

problemText: A right rectangular prism has edge lengths of 2 inches, 3 inches, and 4 inches. Using the formula V = l × w × h, what is the volume of this prism?
hints: Multiply all three edge lengths together.
The volume formula uses all three dimensions, not just two of them.

problemText: A small box measures 1/2 inch long, 1/2 inch wide, and 1/2 inch tall. What is the volume of this box in cubic inches?
hints: Multiply 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 to find the volume.
When you multiply three fractions, multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator.

problemText: A wooden block shaped like a rectangular prism measures 2 inches long, 1/2 inch wide, and 3 inches tall. What is the volume of the block in cubic inches?
hints: Use the formula V = l × w × h with the three given measurements.
When one edge is a fraction and the others are whole numbers, you can still multiply all three together.

problemText: A rectangular prism has edges of 3/4 inch, 2/3 inch, and 1 inch. To pack this prism with unit-fraction cubes that fit evenly along all three edges with no gaps or leftover space, what should the edge length of each small cube be?
hints: The small cube's edge length must divide evenly into 3/4, 2/3, and 1 inch.
Find the largest unit fraction that fits evenly into all three edge lengths.

problemText: A small gift box measures 2 inches long, 3/2 inches wide, and 1/2 inch tall. A student packs this box with unit-fraction cubes that are each 1/2 inch on every edge. After counting that 12 small cubes fit inside, the student multiplies 12 by the volume of one small cube to find the total volume. What volume does the student get?
hints: First find the volume of one small cube with edge length 1/2 inch.
Then multiply the number of small cubes (12) by the volume of each one.

problemText: A rectangular prism has a length of 5/4 inches and a width of 1/2 inch. When this prism is packed with small cubes of edge length 1/4 inch, exactly 20 small cubes fit inside. What is the height of the prism in inches?
hints: Count how many small cubes fit along length and width, then use that to find how many must fit along the height.
The total count of small cubes along all three dimensions should multiply to give 20.
